judgements.justification: Three A reviewers gave 7 and three B reviewers gave 8 for similar assessments, and each area chair set the tier by its mean (7.25 poster, 7.75 spotlight).
B's reviewers rated above the accept level (three 8s), and B's spotlight follows its higher mean, not agreement alone; A had no dissent either.
Scores rose in both committees, on an analytic rate comparison in A and a conceded typo in B; neither rested on unchecked results copied from other papers.
Stage 1 records no weakness that B's meta-review dropped or reversed; B's reviewers themselves called their reservations small, and the tier follows B's scores.
Every checkable reviewer claim in both committees was correct; no score rested on a misreading of the paper.
B's authors conceded only a typo in background prose outside the proofs, not an unfavourable fact about the results.
A's late review (Reviewer_Kz6Q, 18 days after the others) gave 8 with no new objection; no score fell after the response period.
The committees' scores differ (means 7.25 and 7.75), and each area chair followed its own mean, so the split lies in reviewer calibration, not in area-chair cut-offs.
Neither area chair passed over a better-informed dissenting verdict; all reviewers in both committees recommended acceptance at 7 or 8.
The response answered concerns in both committees and moved one reviewer up in each (rN14 in A, v7Aq in B).
Both committees' ratings span only 7 to 8; stage 1 finds no outlier in either.
No reviewer's score stood apart from its committee; Reviewer_CRtT did not reply, but its 7 matched A's other scores.
Neither committee had a low-scoring detractor at the end; B's v7Aq moved from weak reject to 7 and was not set aside.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit; B's area chair called the work of clear interest to the audience.
Stage 1 finds no misstatement in either meta-review; both summarise their reviewers' consensus accurately.

Two of A's four reviewers engaged with the response (rN14 revised, Kz6Q replied), so not most of A left it unanswered, and CRtT's and xAhK's 7s did not stand against answered points that would have moved them.
B's Reviewer_r7mh rated 8 at confidence 2, and Reviewer_KRE1 rated 8 at confidence 5 with no sign of a math check; B's area chair counted both at full weight in the 7.75 mean that set the spotlight.
Neither committee split between accept and reject; all final ratings are 7 or 8.
On Tikhonov's qualification the authors gave A a 'different notation' defence but conceded the error to B, so the two committees saw different accounts of the same point.
Both committees correctly placed the work as an extension of Marteau-Ferey et al.; no novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work.
B's spotlight matches its 7.75 mean and three 8s, and its meta-review cites broad interest; the tier is not unsupported by its scores.
No reviewer objected to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
A's most positive reviewer, Reviewer_Kz6Q, wrote a substantive 8-hour review and replied after the rebuttal, so A also had an engaged champion.
Both committees accepted, and neither judged the promised revisions too large for camera-ready.
Both meta-reviews rest on their visible reviews; no off-record assessment appears.
Both committees judged the paper as a theory contribution on the same terms; neither demanded a different kind of contribution.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score after the rebuttal; all final ratings are 7 or 8.
